nativeApprovalAuthorityOperations.description: One original Native installation/account authority operation per service in the same canonical order. Install, authorize, configure, disable and uninstall change this operation. A startup enable/probe changes the live installation revision but preserves this operation. Native resolves these identifiers from its existing management receipts.

Submission.description: Trusted immutable Native outbox intention. taskId is the existing PublicTask UUID, distinct from localSessionId and Host agentSessionId; null agentSessionId means creation. snapshot.turnOperationId is the actual turn operation, not the separate create submission operation. cwd is Native canonical authority, content blocks reuse existing v2 attachment handling and aggregate limits. Initial model expectedRevision=0 precedes Host record revision=1. Entire typed intention participates in Host HMAC; grant/context expiry and transport request IDs do not. No platform credential/configuration. Nonempty market selection currently requires permissionMode=ask; auto/full returns permission_mode_unavailable with recovery to request approval mode. Empty selection keeps the existing three permission modes.

HelloPayload.description: First frame of the Native-owned pipe. Host instance must equal the existing sidecar startup nonce and PPID watchdog must identify the owning Native process. Only this pipe establishes Native identity; HTTP bearer and Trace cannot.

HelloResult.description: Ready means the Native private authority handshake/control service is available. It does not assert model credentials, Runtime readiness, provider login or qualified tool execution; connector authorization must work independently of model-key availability.

GrantRegisterPayload.description: Native only emits after its current permission lock, SQL31 accepted immutable snapshot, attachment resolution, exact selected installation generation and scope checks. Host retains the complete immutable intention in bounded memory. Platform credentials never enter the pipe.

GrantRegistration.description: Non-secret, generation-bound in-memory lookup only; not a JWT or bearer. No raw content is echoed. Replaying registration returns the same grant and does not extend expiry.

RevokeAuthorityPayload.description: Trusted reducing-authority action. Omit installationId to invalidate all grants/leases in this stable Native scope, otherwise those referencing that installation. Never require still-valid execute permission to revoke. The Native epoch/owner/tenant must still match the pipe owner.

SubmissionReceipt.description: Host durable operation observation. accepted requires actual Host session/Runtime generation/Thread/Turn, returned from native facts. pending/uncertain never fabricate IDs and never trigger a replacement operation. A same-intent accepted replay returns its original receipt before worker prepare/config/Runtime work; changed full intent conflicts.

SubmitPayload.description: HTTP trigger only. The caller cannot replace scope, task, cwd, text, model or selection. An exact previously accepted operation is read before preparation; only a live Native grant may admit new execution.

MarketApproval.description: Independent market approval projection. identity is obtained by trusted Broker query for the real tools/call; never synthesized from metadata/tool title/last Item. Approval state is not provider execution success. New web modes project paired deadlines from Broker. expiresAtUnixMs keeps execution deadline; pending UI/decision uses decisionExpiresAtUnixMs when present, otherwise legacy expiresAtUnixMs. No post-approval extension.

ApprovalDecidePayload.description: Native-owned pipe only after current user decision authorization. Host resolves its real pending authority and exact Broker CallIdentity, validates scope/Turn/revision/expiry and records the one-time decision. No HTTP bearer-only approval route and no old Sorftime route fallback.

ToolObservation.description: Minimal observation from actual native MCP Tool Item facts. Optional service/callRef require explicit trusted correlation; never guess matching Item by latest item, same tool or args. resultText is safe bounded text from actual native output, never raw platform credentials/transport/config. Approval acceptance is not result completion. failed is an unsuccessful native tool observation, not proof that a provider request was sent, not sent or executed. Fixed Gateway error text may distinguish known pre-dispatch rejection from unverified outcome; do not infer this distinction from a generic code or guess callRef linkage. Optional correlation is the bounded Gateway-owned native result metadata. callRef must equal correlation.callRef; thread/turn/tool must match the containing Item and Native must verify the original selection/reference. Unknown/invalid metadata is omitted without losing native facts. service retains its old ProviderBinding type; correlation never contains credentialRef. Read-only decision and admission facts cannot authorize execution or imply provider success. Result text is a common bounded/redacted projection of native content and structuredContent, shared by native notifications and history. Structured-only results use resultText with resultTextSource=structured; different structured JSON is retained in structuredResultText. Identical JSON copies are not duplicated. Combined display bytes stay within maxResultTextBytes; truncated marks actual omitted/truncated content, never merely a second representation.

ErrorCode.description: Safe Host-specific errors plus the exact referenced provider error set. Provider error codes are not copied or independently widened.

NativeObservation.description: Safe scoped Native observation. Optional availableTurns is the latest 128 known native bindings in descending submission order, each with its original selectionDisplay; turnsTruncated reports older bindings omitted from the index. A known requested nativeTurnId is read with its own display snapshot, never the latest selection. Without a current Host, omit remote facts without starting/probing/reconstructing authority. With a current owned Host, historical tool reads validate scope/agent/thread/turn, not the original Host nonce. Approvals always require the current Host nonce. Current remote read failures stay typed errors. Recheck task.read and local view after awaits. Unmanaged sessions need no Host access. Old producers may omit the new index, and old readers may ignore it. No history read restores execution or approval. Optional decisionFacts are original selected-turn read-only Native evidence, available without Host. They do not populate actionable approvals. toolsRead=none omits tools and must not clear previously observed UI tool facts; events consumes notification-derived snapshots; history preserves explicit read/recovery behavior. With an explicit toolsRead mode, unavailable or invalid remote observations are omitted with remoteIssue while scoped local decisionFacts remain readable. This cannot make historical decisions actionable. Legacy omitted toolsRead retains its existing typed remote-error behavior. Active observations prioritize facts for exact currently pending approval/call identities when the history window is truncated. Historical facts otherwise follow append order; observedAtUnixMs is a captured wall-clock value, never an ordering or permission authority.

ObservedTurn.description: Read-only original turn identity and submitted display snapshot. Never an approval or execution grant.

ToolsReadMode.description: none reads approvals/local facts only; events uses a bounded projection of real native notifications, seeding a missing snapshot from native history; history explicitly refreshes native history. Omission retains history behavior. No mode dispatches tools.

DecisionFact.description: Append-only read-only Native decision evidence in the existing scoped conversation database. requested is durable user intent before delivery, acknowledged is an exact validated Host reply, unconfirmed is absence of a verified reply. None proves permit consumption, tool completion or business success. Contains no authority/capability/credential references or raw parameters; never queued, replayed or used to restore approval.
